checks: The denominator h²+2h−1 is positive on the parameter interval, and the numerator of s factors as (1−h)(h²+3h+1). The positive parallel edge lengths give a genuine convex trapezoid. Linear interpolation gives x=±(s+h)/(1+h)=±A at height zero, making zero interior. The top and bottom intersections on x=0 and x+y=0 lie on their asserted edges.

Outside both oblique caps the upper sector requires −y<x<0, which forces y>0. Convexity and containment of the three vertices identify its closure as the radial triangle, with area 1/2. On y≥0 the right side interpolates linearly from x=A to x=0, giving right double area A/2. The reflection (x,y)↦(−x−y,y), of determinant −1, preserves the trapezoid and yields the other upper double area A/2.

The lower double sector is the triangle 0≤x≤−y and −h≤y≤0, with area h²/2. The triple intersection is {0}. The two other unique sectors are reflected quadrilaterals, with common area (|K_h|−1/2−A−h²/2)/2. In particular the right lower unique sector has the extra vertex (s+h,−h) beyond its radial triangle because s>0.

The trapezoid formula and A(h²+2h−1)=1 give |K_h|=3/2+2A−h²/2. Combining the appropriate unique and double sectors gives raw area 1/2+A for each cap. Dividing |K_h| by that raw area and using h²+2h+1=(1+h)² gives the positive denominator D(h).

Differentiation gives D′(h)=2(2−h(1+h)²)/(1+h)² and c′(h)=−D′(h)/D(h)². The function h(1+h)² is strictly increasing with endpoint limits 2(√2−1) and 4, so the unique stationary point is the minimum of c. At the lower endpoint use h²=1−2h and 4/(1+h)=2(1+h) to get D=2. At the upper endpoint D=5−1−2=2. Strict monotonicity on both sides gives the supremum 1/2.

Independent rational shoelace calculations at h=7/10 give 1/2, 50/89, 50/89, 49/200, 14539/17800, 14539/17800 for the six sectors, total 62339/17800, and common fraction 1700/3667. Exact subtraction gives 12−(c+3)²=47267/13446889>0, (9/4)c−1=158/3667>0 and c−128/279=4924/1023093>0. Since c+3>0, the first comparison gives c<2√3−3.

Source 9879e3413b9c4cbf supplies the explicit counterexample and its Balanced trapezoid family. Its label of an interior maximum is reversed by the sign of c′. The frozen statement correctly records a minimum and the endpoint supremum. Its last two inequalities preserve the scope of the source’s numerical comparisons.
